title: From Hourly to Annual: How the Us Minimum Wage Affects Your Pay and Tax
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the us minimum wage of $26.44. Understand tax, super, and fortnightly pay for 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week at the us minimum wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross pay is $52,254.56, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week and then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before deductions.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the base rate set by the Fair Work Commission, currently $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are industry-specific minimums that may be higher and include additional entitlements like casual loading and penalty rates. Always check your award for your correct rate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate?
faqs.a: No, super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) and is not part of your hourly rate. It is an additional contribution to your retirement fund, calculated on your ordinary time earnings up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or are considering a salary offer, the quickest way to compare them is to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees in Australia, the assumed week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So, annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52.

For example, the **us minimum wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. Using the formula: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.56 per year. That is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare, and any other deductions. If you are a casual employee, you typically receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. That loading is meant to compensate for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

It is also helpful to think in fortnightly terms. Your weekly pay at the us minimum wage is $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72. Multiply that by 2 for a fortnightly figure of $2,009.44. Many employers pay fortnightly, so knowing this can help you budget.

### The Us Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor set by the Fair Work Commission. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate. Award rates vary by industry and occupation, and they often include additional penalties for overtime, weekends, or public holidays. The us minimum wage of $26.44 is the baseline; your actual rate may be higher. For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the applicable minimum rate. This loading is meant to cover entitlements like annual leave and sick leave that casuals do not receive. When using our [the timesheet](/) tool, you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it for you. Learn more about [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Income

Once you have your gross annual figure, the next step is to estimate your take-home pay after tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. This means the Medicare levy reduction for low-income earners may be slightly different, but the standard 2% applies to most taxpayers.

For the us minimum wage annual salary of $52,254.56, the tax would be calculated as:
- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($45,000 – $18,200) = $4,020
- 30% on $7,254.56 ($52,254.56 – $45,000) = $2,176.37
- Total tax = $6,196.37
- Medicare levy (2%) = $1,045.09
- Total deductions = $7,241.46
- Estimated take-home pay = $45,013.10 per year, or about $865.64 per week.

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more personalised estimate, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional contribution your employer must make on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12%. It is calculated on your ordinary time earnings (the hours you normally work) and is paid into a super fund of your choice. The super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an extra cost to the employer.

For the us minimum wage example, the annual super contribution would be 12% of $52,254.56 = $6,270.55, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Since $52,254.56 is well below that cap, the full 12% applies. Your total remuneration package (salary plus super) would be $58,525.11. For more on how super interacts with your pay, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Average Earnings Context

It can be useful to compare your pay to broader averages. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, in May 2026 the average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time were $2,083.70 per week. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. The average for all employees (including part-time) was $1,579.20 per week. These figures are higher than the us minimum wage because they include higher-paid roles. For more context, visit our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your hourly rate and instantly see your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly pay. You can also toggle the 25% casual loading checkbox. The tool applies the standard 38-hour week assumption, but you can adjust hours if needed. It then estimates tax and Medicare based on the 2026–27 rates, and shows super paid on top. Remember, this is an estimate and not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability.

### Important Notes

This conversion assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It uses the 2026–27 tax rates and the Medicare levy with the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. The super guarantee is 12% on ordinary earnings up to the maximum contribution base. Always check your specific award or agreement for your correct entitlements. For further reading, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).
